sources.authors: Xu H, Han C, Chen M, Li P, Zhu S, Fang Y, Hu J, Ma H, Lu HD
sources.title: Rivalry-Like Neural Activity in Primary Visual Cortex in Anesthetized Monkeys
sources.key_findings: V1 ocular dominance columns in anesthetized monkeys show 0.03-0.2 Hz antiphase modulation during binocular rivalry stimulation; dominance epoch duration fits gamma distribution (mean 4.3s) matching awake human observers; rivalry-like dynamics occur without consciousness
sources.relevance: Core evidence that V1 local inhibition mechanism operates independently of consciousness; defines V1's role as pre-conscious rivalry generator
sources.quality: high - direct optical imaging, large trial count (n=148), controlled conditions; anesthesia as consciousness knockout

sources.authors: Doesburg SM, Green JJ, McDonald JJ, Ward LM
sources.title: Rhythms of consciousness: binocular rivalry reveals large-scale oscillatory network dynamics mediating visual perception
sources.key_findings: Gamma bursts (35-45 Hz) at 220-280 ms and 540-600 ms before perceptual switch; gamma bursts nested in theta rhythm (4-6 Hz); network involves bilateral DLPFC, right prefrontal, right precuneus, right inferior temporal; one theta cycle (~167-250 ms) may define one 'frame' of consciousness
sources.relevance: Core evidence for large-scale network oscillatory dynamics underlying consciousness switching; theta-gamma coupling as temporal structure of perceptual awareness
sources.quality: medium - EEG has limited spatial resolution; correlational; switch timing may overlap with motor report preparation

sources.title: Seeing the invisible: the scope and limits of unconscious processing in binocular rivalry
sources.key_findings: Simple features (orientation, color, basic motion) show full-strength adaptation aftereffects during suppression; complex features (spiral motion, illusory contours) show near-zero aftereffects; semantic priming disappears during suppression; tool images still activate dorsal pathway (V3A, V7, IPS) while ventral temporal closes; fear faces activate amygdala but ventral temporal closes; proposed 'fragile unconscious binding hypothesis'
sources.relevance: Establishes hierarchical gradient of consciousness-dependence for visual processing; defines scope of unconscious vs conscious visual computation
sources.quality: high - integrates multiple independent labs' findings; adaption aftereffect paradigm is well-validated; reviewed multiple experimental modalities

sources.title: Single units and conscious vision
sources.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological Sciences
sources.key_findings: V1 neurons mostly fire to retinal stimulus not perception during suppression; perception-neural correlation increases up the hierarchy (V1→V4→MT→IT); IT cortex shows ~90% perception-correlated activity; cells influencing perception are almost exclusively binocular cells; proportion of binocular cells increases with hierarchy level
sources.relevance: Landmark single-unit study establishing hierarchical gradient of consciousness-neural correlation; foundational evidence against single-locus 'consciousness gate'
sources.quality: high - single-cell recording with behavioral report in trained monkey; multi-area comparison; landmark paper with >3000 citations

sources.authors: Li HH, Rankin J, Rinzel J, Carrasco M, Heeger DJ
sources.title: Attention model of binocular rivalry
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.key_findings: EEG competition index drops near zero when attention is diverted by high cognitive load task; computational model combining attention scaling + mutual inhibition + slow adaptation reproduces Levelt's second proposition (revised); rivalry requires active attention; not a purely automatic sensory process
sources.relevance: Core evidence that attention is a necessary component of binocular rivalry, challenging automatic-rivalry assumption; computational model integrates attention with classical rivalry mechanisms
sources.quality: medium - EEG SSVEP measure is well-established; dual-task confound (attention vs arousal/load); attention necessity vs strong modulation still debated

sources.title: Visual competition
sources.notes: Abstract only; comprehensive review of binocular rivalry mechanisms; widely cited framework paper
sources.key_findings: Rivalry involves 'a succession of processes, each implemented by neural mechanisms at different levels of the visual hierarchy' rather than a single mechanism
sources.relevance: Provides the fundamental multi-level framework consensus for binocular rivalry mechanisms; most-cited review in the field
sources.quality: high - Nature Reviews, collaborative review by two leading researchers; landmark framework paper

sources.authors: Tong F, Nakayama K, Vaughan JT, Kanwisher N
sources.title: Binocular rivalry and visual awareness in human extrastriate cortex
sources.notes: Abstract only; face-house binocular rivalry fMRI paradigm
sources.key_findings: FFA and PPA activity tracks perception (which image is conscious) not retinal input (which eye is stimulated); response magnitude matches non-rivalry alternation; high-level visual cortex represents perceived not retinal content
sources.relevance: Direct fMRI evidence that ventral temporal cortex (FFA/PPA) reflects conscious perception content; landmark human fMRI binocular rivalry study
sources.quality: high - well-controlled fMRI experiment; exploits categorical selectivity of FFA/PPA as independent markers; highly cited

sources.title: Interocular rivalry revealed in the human cortical blind-spot representation
sources.notes: Abstract only; ingenious use of physiological blind spot for monocular V1 access
sources.key_findings: fMRI activity in monocular V1 region corresponding to blind spot tracks perceptual dominance during binocular rivalry; suggests V1 participates in selection and expression of conscious visual information
sources.relevance: Evidence that V1, under specific conditions (monocular blind spot region), correlates with conscious perception; complicates simple 'V1 is pre-conscious' view
sources.quality: medium-high - Nature publication; clever anatomical exploitation; fMRI spatial limitations for small V1 region; needs replication

sources.authors: Yilmaz P, Stein T, Sterzer P, Hesselmann G
sources.title: The complexity of human subjective experience during binocular rivalry
sources.notes: Abstract only; phenomenological categorization of perceptual switch types
sources.key_findings: Identified 20 distinct perceptual switch categories during binocular rivalry; participants reported 2-3 types per stimulus presentation on average; traditional paradigms likely severely underestimate phenomenological complexity of rivalry
sources.relevance: Methodological critique of standard binary (A/B) reporting paradigms; suggests neural correlate studies may be missing important experiential content
sources.quality: medium - recent 2025 paper, Neuroscience of Consciousness; phenomenological categorization methodology is novel; implications for neural studies are indirect

note: Full text read via PMC open access: Xu 2016 (PMC6705522), Doesburg 2009 (PMC2702101), Lin & He 2009 (PMC2689366), Logothetis 1998 (PMC1692419), Li 2017 (PMC5544261). Abstract-only: Blake & Logothetis 2002, Tong et al. 1998, Tong & Engel 2001, Yilmaz et al. 2025.
